subject: AsterBank RFI: SIG/ISO Artifact Capture Playbook and Ownership
messages:
From: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@asterbank.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@asterbank.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial intake: SIG/ISO artifact capture needs

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this. As part of AsterBank's RFI we need a pragmatic "artifact capture playbook" that maps SIG control families to the evidence you can produce, who at Redwood will be the owner for collection, and recommended collection cadence for high-volume logs. Our procurement team also wants to understand how you scale evidence collection across multiple business units without overwhelming our internal stakeholders.

High-level asks:
- Control crosswalk (SIG + ISO21001-ish mapping)
- Owner matrix (who at Redwood collects each artifact / who we'll contact)
- Sampling / log extraction guidance for high-volume systems (tokenization, PII redaction)
- Expected timelines for delivery of packaged evidence

Can you confirm you can provide a draft playbook and a short weekly cadence for collection? Ideally we want something we can include in the RFI response by 2026-08-17.

Also looping in our external security assessor (AuditOps) for technical scoping.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Reyes
Head of IT Risk, AsterBank
From: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
To: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@asterbank.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@asterbank.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: SIG/ISO artifact capture needs

Daniel — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver a pragmatic playbook and an owner matrix. Proposed immediate plan:

1) Kickoff call (30 min) to align scope and sampling thresholds — propose 2026-08-05 10:00 PT.
2) We will produce: a) control crosswalk (SIG -> SOC2/ISO mapping) b) artifact capture playbook PDF c) owner matrix spreadsheet.
3) For high-volume logs we’ll provide sampling & redaction guidance plus a short script to produce a sanitized sample.

I’ve attached a short draft crosswalk (redwood_control_crosswalk_v1.xlsx) and an internal playbook outline. Markus (ops lead) is on copy; Neha (assurance) will own artifact packaging.

Attachments: redwood_control_crosswalk_v1.xlsx (Excel, 280KB)

Next: please confirm the kickoff slot or suggest an alternate and any specific regulatory constraints (e.g., data residency or encryption requirements).

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@asterbank.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-05T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: SIG/ISO artifact capture needs

Thanks all — quick notes from our side after internal review (for the kickoff):

- Control crosswalk: the attached workbook contains a SIG family tab and a mapped SOC2/ISO row for each control. Where we have standard artifacts (e.g., SOC2 report, network diagrams, KMS attestation) they are flagged as "standard deliverable."
- Owners: I’ll take operational artifacts (runtime logs, deployment manifests). Neha will own assurance artifacts (policy docs, SOC2 bridge statements). Tessa will coordinate delivery.
- Sampling: recommend 7-day rolling tokenized log extract for high-throughput services; we can provide a small anonymization script (Python) and a gzipped sample.
- Timeline: Draft playbook + owner matrix by 2026-08-10, final packet by 2026-08-16 if all artifacts collected.

Attachment: architecture-diagram.png (PNG, 450KB)

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Production Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@asterbank.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@asterbank.com>, security@auditops.com
Date: 2026-08-06T08:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: SIG/ISO artifact capture needs

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from InfoSec & Procurement:
- We need to confirm whether log extracts can be produced with AsterBank-specific identifiers pseudonymized (we cannot accept raw PII).
- For the SOC2 bridge we asked for the last 12 months of evidence where applicable — can you scope what is "reasonable" to provide vs. what we should expect to validate in-person?
- On timelines: procurement needs any dependencies called out (e.g., legal review for DPA amendments).

Can the anonymization script be run by our team or does it require Redwood to run and deliver?

Thanks,
Priya Singh
Senior Procurement Manager, AsterBank
From: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@asterbank.com>, Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@asterbank.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-06T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: SIG/ISO artifact capture needs

Priya — good questions. Short answers:

- Pseudonymization: yes. The sample script can be run by your team (we’ll supply a containerized job) or we can run it and deliver the sanitized bundle. Either approach is fine; we prefer you run it for full control over environment.
- SOC2 bridge: we will delineate standard deliverables (SOC2 report, system description, KMS attestation) vs. on-demand artifacts (raw logs). For raw logs we will provide sanitized samples covering the requested 12-month windows where feasible — typically rolling 7-day extracts across key change windows. Anything beyond that will be scoped as an additional collection activity.
- Dependencies: DPA/legal review for audit access, any third-party consents for 3rd-party hosted services, and scheduling windows for runtime exports.

Neha — can you confirm packaging format (preferred: single ZIP with index.html manifest) and whether we can include checksums?

Thanks,
Tessa
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, Priya Singh <priya.singh@asterbank.com>, Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@asterbank.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-07T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: SIG/ISO artifact capture needs

Confirmed — packaging approach and small operational notes:

- Packaging: single ZIP per control-family with an index.html manifest listing artifacts, source, owner, and SHA256 checksum. We will include a README with redaction notes.
- Evidence retention: our standard evidence bundle contains artifacts covering the latest SOC2 period; for older windows we include sampling notes and retention proofs (where logs are ephemeral, we include retention policies and archival proof).
- Access model: we can either: a) deliver via SFTP with time-limited credentials, b) provide a signed download link from our secure artifacts bucket, or c) ship on encrypted media for on-prem requests.

Attachment: access-log-sample.txt (TXT, 45KB)

Neha Kapoor
Assurance Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@asterbank.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@asterbank.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com, security@auditops.com
Date: 2026-08-10T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: SIG/ISO artifact capture needs — playbook received

Team — thanks for the playbook and owner matrix. The packaged PDF and spreadsheet arrived via the Drive link. A couple follow-ups before we finalize in the RFI:

- Can you explicitly call out which artifacts require legal sign-off before export (I expect DB snapshots, full auth logs).
- Please confirm whether encryption-at-rest keys are customer-specific or managed by Redwood (we need to note this in control mapping).
- AuditOps will schedule a short technical review next week; they may request a short live demo of the anonymization pipeline.

If you can update the playbook with those two clarifications by EOD 2026-08-12 we can finalize our RFI package.

Thanks,
Daniel
---
Daniel Reyes
Head of IT Risk, AsterBank

[Attachment: redwood_control_capture_playbook.pdf (PDF, 340KB)]
